name: window_onload
purpose: Boot routine for the frameset shell page. Sets up global references, decides whether this is a policy / search / utility shell, sizes the frame rows/cols, loads the security data island, and kicks off the serial (menu-then-tree-then-page) load.
legacy:
Sub window_onload
  On Error Resume Next
  AddWindowToCollection window
  Set GlobalVars = New globalVarsClass
  Set mobjAQSMain = window
  Set mobjParentWindow = window.opener
  If mblnReplacementHomePage Then ... rebuild child-window refs ...
  document.body.setAttribute "policyid", mstrPolicyID
  If CLng(mstrPolicyID) > 0 Then fraHorizontal.rows="46,*": fraTreeColumn.rows="90,*"
  ElseIf CLng(mstrPolicyID)=0 Then mblnSearchPage=True ...
  Set mxmlSecurity = CreateObject("MSXML2.DOMDocument.6.0")
  mxmlSecurity.loadXML(document.all("xdiSecurity").XMLDocument.xml)
  Call ExecuteAction("menu", "POL|POL|" & mstrExpiredNumber & "|", -1, "")
End Sub
explanation: This is the one routine in the section with real, working React code. shellLoad + useShellLoad reproduce the boot sequence: resolveShellMode replaces the CLng(mstrPolicyID) branch that chose policy vs. search vs. utility layout, resolveInitialAction replaces the mstrAction/-3 logic, and the security XML island is parsed once into auth-store instead of an MSXML DOMDocument. The frame-sizing lines (fraHorizontal.rows, fraVertical.cols) are gone because the SPA uses CSS layout, not a frameset. The kickoff call to ExecuteAction('menu', ...) is preserved as executeAction, which begins the serial page load.

name: LoadNextPage
purpose: Second step of the serial load. The menu frame calls this from its own onload to load the tree (or the next page), deliberately staggered to avoid the browser trying to load every frame at once.
legacy:
Sub LoadNextPage()
  If StrComp(Left(mstrNodeKey, 3), "SYS", 0) = 0 Then
    Call ExecuteAction(mstrAction, mstrNodeKey, 0, "")   ' utilities
  Else
    Select Case UCase(Left(mstrNodeKey,7))
      Case "POL|POL"
        ' load tree BEFORE first page for policy windows
        Call ExecuteAction("TREE", "POL|POL|" & mstrExpiredNumber & "|", -1, "")
      Case Else
        Call ExecuteAction(mstrAction, "POL|POL|" & mstrExpiredNumber & "|", 0, "")
    End Select
  End If
End Sub
reactHome: would live in: engine/load/shell-load.ts (+ config/routes.ts route loaders)
explanation: The reason this routine exists at all — 'prevent timing problems caused by loading all the pages at once' — is a frameset artifact, so the callback-chaining mechanism is eliminated. What survives is the ordering decision: for a policy shell load the tree before the first page; for SYS utilities just load the action directly. In React that ordering is expressed as sequential awaits inside the shell loader (or nested React Router route loaders) rather than a frame calling back into the parent. The branch logic itself still needs to be built, so this is a design mapping, not shipped code.

name: LoadFirstPage
purpose: Third and final step of the serial load. The tree frame calls this from its onload to load the first content page the user actually sees, then (for real policies) polls the menu for umbrella-mapping status.
legacy:
Sub LoadFirstPage
  On Error Resume Next
  Call ExecuteAction(mstrAction, "POL|POL|" & mstrExpiredNumber & "|", 0, "")
  Call TrapBrowserError("LoadFirstPage|1")
  If mstrPolicyID <> "0" Then
    window.setTimeout "document.frames(""menu"").FetchUmbrellaMappingStatus()", 1000, "vbscript"
  End If
End Sub
explanation: This is the payoff of the staggered chain: load the first page the user sees via ExecuteAction. In React it is simply the last await in the shell load sequence. The setTimeout(...,1000) that reaches across into document.frames('menu') to call FetchUmbrellaMappingStatus is a classic IE cross-frame timing hack — with no frames it becomes an ordinary async call or effect, so the 1-second delay is eliminated. The routine is a design mapping today: the first-page load routes through the scaffolded execute-action.ts, but this specific tail step and the umbrella-status fetch are not yet wired.

name: ClearActionMenus
purpose: Forces the per-LOB action menus (button bars) to reload after a rate-level change by pointing their frames at blank.htm. Given a nodekey it clears just that LOB's menu; with no nodekey it clears all action-type frames.
legacy:
Sub ClearActionMenus(pstrNodeKey)
  On Error Resume Next
  If Len(pstrNodeKey) > 0 Then
    Set objFrames = fraMain.children(GetActionMenuNameException(pstrNodeKey))
    If Not objFrames Is Nothing Then objFrames.src = "../../system/htm/blank.htm"
  Else
    Set objFrames = fraMain.children   ' all action frames
    ' <GAP: loop that blanks each action frame's src>
  End If
End Sub
explanation: The mechanism here — setting a frame's src to blank.htm to make it reload — is pure frames-era plumbing and is eliminated. The intent, 'a rate-level change happened, so the action menus (buttons) are now stale, reload them,' survives as cache invalidation: mark the ButtonsRenderer data for one LOB (or all LOBs) stale and let it refetch. The nodekey-to-LOB mapping that GetActionMenuNameException did becomes a small lobFromNodeKey helper. Not built yet, so this is a design mapping.

name: IsEmptyEval
purpose: A VBScript workaround: safely test whether an expression/variable is defined. Eval of an undefined name raises error 450, so this traps that error and reports whether the name existed.
legacy:
Function IsEmptyEval(value)
  On Error Resume Next
  IsEmpty(Eval(value))
  If Err.Number = 450 Then emptyCheck = False Else emptyCheck = True
  On Error GoTo 0
  IsEmptyEval = emptyCheck
End Function
explanation: This exists only to work around VBScript's behaviour where Eval-ing an undefined identifier throws error 450 instead of returning empty. Its sole caller, AddWindowToCollection, uses it to check whether window.opener exposes an AddWindowToCollection method. In JavaScript that check is a one-liner (typeof opener?.addWindowToCollection === 'function' or optional chaining), so the entire helper disappears. Marked eliminated: there is nothing to port.

name: AddWindowToCollection
purpose: Registers a window in a global Scripting.Dictionary shared across all app windows. It walks up through openers to the top-most window that owns the collection, so every window can later be found and closed (e.g. on logout) even if the home window is gone.
legacy:
Sub AddWindowToCollection(myWindow)
  If Not IsEmpty(myWindow) Then
    If IsObject(window.opener) And Not IsEmptyEval("window.opener.AddWindowToCollection") Then
      window.opener.AddWindowToCollection myWindow      ' bubble up to top owner
    Else
      windowsCollection.Add CStr(windowsCollection.Count), myWindow
      Set myWindow.windowsCollection = windowsCollection ' share ref down to all windows
    End If
  End If
End Sub
explanation: The whole reason this recursively bubbles up through window.opener is that each browser window in the old app has its own script context, so they must nominate one top window to hold the master list and then share the Dictionary reference back down. A single-page React app has one JS context, so the window-manager module already IS the single shared registry — the opener-walking and reference-propagation collapse to a plain map insert. window-manager.ts exists as a scaffolded registry keyed one-per-window, which is the right home; this specific add-and-share behaviour maps onto it directly but the logout-time enumeration it feeds is not fully built.

name: LogoutMain
purpose: Logout handler for the Home page. Closes every tracked window — external windows, policy child windows, and non-policy child windows — then closes itself and sets the logout flag.
legacy:
Function LogoutMain()
  If Not mdicExternalWindows Is Nothing Then
    For intCount = 0 To mdicExternalWindows.Count - 1
      Set objWindowLogoutMain = arrWindowsMain(intCount)
      If Not objWindowLogoutMain.closed Then objWindowLogoutMain.close
    Next
  End If
  ' ... same loop for mdicChildWindows and mdicNonPolicyChildWindows ...
  window.close
  mblnLogout = True
End Function
explanation: Three near-identical loops walk the external / policy-child / non-policy-child dictionaries and close each still-open window. In React those three dictionaries collapse into the single window-manager registry, so this becomes windowManager.closeAll() plus an auth-store logout that raises the mblnLogout flag. window-manager.ts is scaffolded as a registry but its closeAll enumeration and the auth-store logout are not yet built, so this is a design mapping. Note that actual OS-level window.close of separate browser windows has no SPA analogue — 'windows' become in-app modals/tabs that are simply unmounted.

name: Logout
purpose: Logout handler invoked from a policy window rather than Home. It reaches up to the parent (home) window and closes all of its external, child, and non-policy child windows, then calls LogoutGrandParent and closes the parent, finally setting the logout flag.
legacy:
Function Logout()
  If Not mobjParentWindow Is Nothing Then
   If Not mobjParentWindow.closed Then
    ' close mobjParentWindow.mdicExternalWindows (loop)
    ' close mobjParentWindow.mdicChildWindows (loop)
    ' close mobjParentWindow.mdicNonPolicyChildWindows (loop)
   End If
   LogoutGrandParent()
   mobjParentWindow.close
  End If
  mblnLogout = True
End Function
explanation: This is the sibling of LogoutMain: same close-everything intent, but written for the case where the user clicked Logout inside a policy window, so it dereferences mobjParentWindow (the home window) and even LogoutGrandParent to climb the opener chain. That entire parent/grandparent hierarchy is an artifact of multiple independent browser windows; in a single-context SPA there is one registry and one session, so both LogoutMain and Logout converge to the same closeAll + auth-store.logout. Marked design — the window-manager close path and auth-store logout still need to be built, and the cross-window opener walking is eliminated.

name: LogoutGrandParent
purpose: When Logout is clicked on a deeply-nested (grand-child) popup, walk up two window levels and close every tracked popup on the grandparent window, then close the grandparent itself.
legacy:
Function LogoutGrandParent()
  If Not mobjParentWindow Is Nothing Then
    If StrComp(Left(mobjParentWindow.name,6),"policy")=0 Then
      Set objGrandParentWindow = mobjParentWindow.opener
      ' close every tracked popup on the grandparent:
      For each objWindow in mdicExternalWindows.Items : objWindow.close : Next
      For each objWindow in mdicChildWindows.Items : objWindow.close : Next
      For each objWindow in mdicNonPolicyChildWindows.Items : objWindow.close : Next
      objGrandParentWindow.close
explanation: The flat window registry means a single closeAll() replaces the two-level window.opener walk and the three parallel dictionaries the legacy code iterates. closeAll() is scaffolded and covers the surviving intent (logout closes every tracked window). The multi-window opener cascade itself is an IE-frameset artifact that the SPA does not reproduce.

name: ShowBatchEdits

The command store is scaffolded, but there is no batch-edits view or the open/close-when-empty logic yet, so this is a plan. The unique-named popup window and the URL-carried policy id are eliminated in the modal design.

name: ShowConversionReport
purpose: If a conversion report id is set (mlngConversionReportID > 0), open a modeless dialog (ConversionSummaryDisplay.asp) showing the policy-conversion summary, then reset the id so it displays only once.

name: LoadWindowReferences
purpose: Register (or replace) a reference to an open policy child window in the mdicChildWindows dictionary, keyed by a string, so the parent can later refocus or close it.
legacy:
Sub LoadWindowReferences(ByVal pstrKey, ByRef pobjWindow)
  If mdicChildWindows Is Nothing Then Set mdicChildWindows = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
  If mdicChildWindows.Exists(CStr(pstrKey)) Then mdicChildWindows.Remove(CStr(pstrKey))
  mdicChildWindows.Add CStr(pstrKey), pobjWindow
explanation: The Map<string, Window> registry in window-manager.ts is exactly this add-or-replace dictionary, and open() already performs registry.delete then registry.set. This is scaffolded. The legacy need to pass the whole Dictionary object between parent and child windows is a frameset artifact that is eliminated by having one registry in one process.

name: LoadNonPolicyWindowReferences
purpose: Same as LoadWindowReferences but for non-policy child windows, tracked in a separate mdicNonPolicyChildWindows dictionary.
legacy:
Sub LoadNonPolicyWindowReferences(ByVal pstrKey, ByRef pobjWindow)
  If mdicNonPolicyChildWindows Is Nothing Then Set ... = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
  If ...Exists(CStr(pstrKey)) Then ...Remove(CStr(pstrKey))
  mdicNonPolicyChildWindows.Add CStr(pstrKey), pobjWindow
explanation: The single registry replaces three parallel dictionaries; the policy vs non-policy distinction collapses into a key prefix. open()/registry.set already provides the tracking, so this is scaffolded. Maintaining a separate Map per window category is unnecessary bookkeeping that is eliminated.

name: LoadExternalWindowReferences
purpose: Register an 'external' window reference; if the current window is a policy window it stores the reference on the parent window's mdicExternalWindows dictionary, otherwise on its own.
legacy:
Sub LoadExternalWindowReferences(ByVal pstrKey, ByRef pobjWindow)
  windowName = pobjWindow.name  ' probe cross-window access
  If StrComp(Left(window.name,6),"policy")=0 Then
    mobjParentWindow.mdicExternalWindows.Add CStr(pstrKey), pobjWindow
  Else
    mdicExternalWindows.Add CStr(pstrKey), pobjWindow
explanation: In a single process there is no separate parent window to defer storage to, so the entire 'am I a policy window, push onto my opener's dictionary' branch is eliminated. The tracking intent is covered by open()/registry.set, so this is scaffolded. The cross-window access probe (reading pobjWindow.name under On Error Resume Next) is an IE-ism that disappears.

name: ParentWindow_Navigate
purpose: Acts as a Back button: if this is a policy window, focus its parent (the search/start page), reopening that search page via XmlCycling.aspx if the parent was closed; otherwise just focus the current window.
legacy:

    Else window.open "../../system/asp/XmlCycling.aspx?...action=main&nodekey=pol|pol|0|&redirect=..."

reactHome: would live in: config/routes.ts (React Router) / a nav action
explanation: In a single-page app there is no separate parent window to focus or re-spawn; 'back to the search page' is just a route change. React Router is wired in the POC (routes.ts), but this specific back-to-search behavior is not implemented. The reopen-via-XmlCycling path and its replacement=t child-window re-parenting handoff are eliminated.

name: ShowFrame
purpose: Switches which frameset row is visible (MAIN for data entry, START for recall, or an LOB action-menu frame) by setting every frame height to 0 except the selected one to '*', clears the data-changed flags, toggles whether the tree is enabled, and retitles the window.
legacy:
Sub ShowFrame(ByVal pstrFrame)
  mblnDataChanged=False : Call SessionXML_ClearItem("datachanged")
  For each frame in fraMain.children:  build "0,0,*,0,..." (* for pstrFrame; tabIndex 1/-1)
  fraMain.rows = strFrameRowSizes
  mstrCurrentFrame = pstrFrame
  If pstrFrame="MAIN" Then Tree_SetState(False) Else Tree_SetState(True)
  Call SetFrameTitle()
explanation: The three frameset configurations are already modeled as a ShellMode enum via resolveShellMode (shipped), and clearing mblnDataChanged maps directly to appStore.setDirty(false). But the full behavior — swapping the rendered layout, disabling the tree on MAIN, and calling SetFrameTitle — is not yet assembled in a shell component, so overall this is scaffolded. The literal fraMain.rows pixel-string manipulation and tabIndex juggling are eliminated.

name: SetFrameTitle

The 'windowtitle' value is exactly the string this migration intends to serve from the Navigation API instead of the heavy per-page user-permissions call, then read from authStore useroptions and applied in an effect. It is straightforward to build but not built.

name: RefreshTree
purpose: Rebuilds the left navigation tree by reaching into the 'tree' frame and calling its Build_Tree method with the root node key POL|POL|0| in LOADTREE mode.
legacy:
Sub RefreshTree()
  Set objDoc = document.frames("tree")
  Call objDoc.Build_Tree("POL|POL|0|", "LOADTREE")
  Set objDoc = Nothing
reactHome: would live in: config/routes.ts (route-loader revalidation) / a Tree component
explanation: The tree is rendered from navigation data, but the POC has no dedicated Tree component or refresh action yet (DataGridRenderer handles XmlList grids, not the nav tree), so this is a plan. Refreshing becomes invalidating the navigation query/loader rather than reaching cross-frame into a 'tree' frame and calling its Build_Tree method. The document.frames("tree") cross-frame call is an eliminated IE-ism.

name: DeleteAction
purpose: Deletes a policy node on the server, and on success removes it from the left-hand tree and refreshes the sibling/parent branches that the deletion affects (line-of-business specific).
legacy:
Sub DeleteAction(ByVal pstrNodeKey, ByVal pstrAction)
  strQueryString = "?object=DELETE&nodekey=" & Escape(SetExpiredNumber(pstrNodeKey)) & "&action=" & pstrAction & "&userid=" & mstrUserID ...
  Set objResponse = CreateObject("MSXML2.DOMDocument.6.0")
  objResponse.load "../../system/ASP/XmlServercall.aspx" & strQueryString
  If status = "ERROR" Then ShowUserMessage(...) / ShowBatchEdits(...)
  ElseIf status = "SUCCESS" Then
     Set objDoc = document.frames("tree")
     objDoc.Remove_TreeNode pstrNodeKey, ""
     Select Case UCase(strLOB)   'BOP/KRM/LIA/PRP/CAU/PAU/INM/WOR
        ... objDoc.Build_Tree(strNodeKey,"LOADBRANCH")
        ... objDoc.Remove_TreeNodeIfNoChildren(strNodeKey)
     End Select
     GlobalVars.mblnPolicyRated = False
reactHome: would live in: engine/commands/execute-action.ts (DELETE handler) + engine/api/client.ts (navigate) + a tree store
explanation: In the legacy shell this is one big action: a synchronous MSXML call to XmlServercall.aspx, then direct DOM surgery on the separate 'tree' frame (Remove_TreeNode / Build_Tree / Remove_TreeNodeIfNoChildren) with a large Select Case of per-line-of-business rules deciding which neighbouring branches to reload. In React the server call becomes an async api.navigate on the shared client, and the tree becomes state: you remove the node from the tree store and re-fetch only the branches the deletion touched, letting the renderer re-draw. The scaffolded execute-action.ts/dispatch.ts give the command-routing skeleton, but this DELETE flow and its LOB-specific branch-refresh table are not built yet, so it is a design.

name: CheckForAsynchProcess
purpose: Asks the server whether a long-running background (asynchronous) process is already in progress for this node/action, and returns that yes/no to the caller so it can decide whether to show a progress bar.
legacy:
Sub CheckForAsynchProcess(ByVal pstrNodeKey, ByVal pstrAction, ByRef pblnProgressBar)
  pblnProgressBar = False
  strQueryString = "?object=CHECKASYNCH&nodekey=" & Escape(SetExpiredNumber(pstrNodeKey)) & "&action=" & pstrAction & "&userid=" & mstrUserID ...
  Set objResponse = CreateObject("MSXML2.DOMDocument.6.0")
  objResponse.async = False
  objResponse.load "../../system/ASP/xmlCheckAsynch.asp" & strQueryString
  Set objNode = .selectSingleNode("//results")
  If StrComp(objNode.Text, "ASYNCHPROGRESSBAR", vbTextCompare) = 0 Then
     pblnProgressBar = True
reactHome: would live in: engine/api/client.ts (checkAsyncProcess call) with progress-bar state in app-store.ts
explanation: This is a small pre-flight probe: a synchronous MSXML request to xmlCheckAsynch.asp whose only result is a flag, returned through a VBScript ByRef out-parameter. In React the ByRef out-parameter becomes a normal Promise<boolean> returned from an async client call, and the 'is a progress bar needed' flag becomes progress state in app-store.ts rather than a variable the caller passes in by reference. It maps cleanly onto the api client pattern but no CHECKASYNCH endpoint or caller exists in the POC yet, so it is a design, not built.

name: ExecuteAction
purpose: The master navigation router: given an action + node key, it asks the server where to go, then decides whether the target renders in the MAIN frame, a side frame, a modal dialog, or a new browser window.
legacy:
Sub ExecuteAction(ByVal pstrAction, pstrNodeKey, pintTab, pstrXMLDetail)
  ' DELETE -> confirm, then DeleteAction
  ' ACTION already loaded -> ShowFrame + RefreshCurrentPage : Exit Sub
  strQueryString = "?nodekey=...&action=...&tab=...&returntype=XML"
  objResponse.load "XmlCycling.aspx" & strQueryString   ' resolve url + frame
  strURL = url & qs : strFrame = UCase(GetNodeText(objNode,"frame"))
  Select Case UCase(strFrame)
    Case "MODAL","MODELESS": window.showModalDialog(strURL, ...)
    Case "NEWWINDOW":        Call OpenNewWindow(strURL, name, options)
    Case "HIDDEN":           objFrame.src = strURL
    Case Else: GetFrameReference(strFrame).src = strURL : ShowFrame(strFrame)
  End Select
  Call UpdateToolBar
End Sub
explanation: This is the single choke-point for 'the user did something'. The legacy version fetches routing from XmlCycling.aspx (returns a url + a frame name) and mutates frame .src / opens dialogs; the React port calls api.pageLayout() and then a switch on result.frame routes to React Router (MAIN), the modal host store (MODAL), or the window manager (NEWWINDOW). The POC file exists and captures the frame switch, but branches like DELETE-confirmation, the -1/90-99 preload/refresh tab codes, MODELESS, HIDDEN, and the deferred-navigation-after-modal handshake are not built yet.

name: FocusBatchEditWindow
purpose: Brings an already-open 'batch edit' popup window back to the foreground (focus) instead of opening a duplicate, keyed by edit type + policy id.
legacy:
Sub FocusBatchEditWindow(ByVal batchEditType)

    If mdicChildWindows.Exists("batcheditdisplay" & batchEditType & Cstr(mstrPolicyID)) Then
      Set objWindow = mdicChildWindows.Item("batcheditdisplay" & batchEditType & Cstr(mstrPolicyID))

The window-manager registry (Map<key, Window>) already implements exactly this reuse-and-focus behaviour, so the mechanism is present. What is not wired is the batch-edit-specific key convention and the post-modal-close trigger (legacy fires it via window.setTimeout 500ms after ExecuteAction) — a small React effect on the modal host would replace the timing hack.

name: GetActionMenuNameException
purpose: Derives the correct action-menu target name from a node key. Normally it is just the first '|'-delimited element, but BOP lines need a program-type suffix taken from the 4th (or 5th, for special coverages) element.
legacy:
Function GetActionMenuNameException(pstrNodeKey)
  strFrame = GetStringField(pstrNodeKey,1,"|")        ' e.g. "BOP"
  If StrComp(strFrame,"BOP",vbTextCompare) = 0 Then
    If Left(GetStringField(pstrNodeKey,2,"|"),3) = "SPC" Then
      strFrame = strFrame & GetStringField(pstrNodeKey,5,"|")  ' 5th elem
    Else
      strFrame = strFrame & GetStringField(pstrNodeKey,4,"|")  ' 4th elem
    End If
  End If
  GetActionMenuNameException = strFrame
End Function
explanation: This is pure node-key string parsing that maps a tree node to the right line-of-business/program-type bucket. In React the OUTPUT is no longer a frame id (frames are gone) but a key into the LOB registry that selects which config/route/renderer to use, so the parsing logic carries over 1:1 while the thing it names changes. It is not built yet — the LOB registry exists, but this BOP 4th/5th-element exception resolver is a design item to add there.

name: GetFrameReference
purpose: Returns the DOM frame with the given id, and if it does not exist, clones the hidden 'action' frame, renames it, and injects it into the frameset — so any number of business-line frames can exist without being predefined in HTML.
legacy:
Function GetFrameReference(pstrFrame)
  Set objFrame = document.all(pstrFrame)
  If Not objFrame Is Nothing Then
    Set GetFrameReference = objFrame
  Else                                   ' create it on the fly
    Set objNewFrame = document.all("action").cloneNode(True)
    objNewFrame.id = pstrFrame
    fraMain.insertBefore(objNewFrame)
    Set GetFrameReference = document.all(pstrFrame)
  End If
End Function
reactHome: eliminated (replaced by config/routes.ts React Router + engine/renderers/FormRenderer)
explanation: This routine exists only because the legacy shell is a frameset and needs arbitrary, dynamically-created frames per business line. A React single-page app has no frames at all — each 'frame' becomes a routed/conditionally-mounted component, and the browser (React) manages mounting/unmounting instead of cloneNode + insertBefore. There is nothing to port; the capability is absorbed by the router and renderers.

name: UpdateToolBar
purpose: After navigation, tells the toolbar/menu to re-evaluate its button enabled/disabled states by reaching into the 'menu' frame and invoking that page's UpdateToolBarButtons script.
legacy:

    Set objDoc = document.frames("menu")
    If Not objDoc Is Nothing Then

In React the toolbar is just a component subscribed to the page/auth stores, so it re-renders on its own whenever button state changes — the explicit 'go update the toolbar now' call disappears. The plumbing that feeds it (dispatch.ts already routes SET_DISABLED/SET_VISIBLE into the page store) is scaffolded, but the ButtonsRenderer/toolbar component that consumes it is not built yet, so this is a design item.

name: RefreshSelectedPage
purpose: Tells a page living inside a (possibly hidden) frame to refresh itself with the current tree/policy data by locating and invoking that page's own RefreshPage script.

name: ExecuteBrowserCommands
purpose: The client-side interpreter for the server's reply. After every server round-trip the server returns a list of 'browser commands' (verb / noun / addinf / resfil); this one loop executes ALL of them in order - showing/hiding/enabling/requiring controls, loading combo boxes, popping messages, questions and modals, navigating, refreshing lists, and updating the nav tree.
legacy:
Sub ExecuteBrowserCommands(ByRef objControl, ByRef objCallingWindow)
  With objCallingWindow
    If Not .mxmlBrowserCtl Is Nothing ... Then
      Set objCalls = .mxmlBrowserCtl.selectNodes("//call")
      For intRtnCount = 0 To objCalls.length - 1
        strVerb=..GetNamedItem("verb")..  ' also noun, addinf, resfil
        If .mblnDoBrowserCommands Then
          If strResFil="" Or strResFil=intResponseFilter Then
            Select Case UCase(strVerb)
              Case "ADD_LISTITEM" / "CLEAR_COMBO" / "LOAD_COMBO" ...
              Case "DISPLAY_ERROR"/"DISPLAY_MESSAGE"/"DISPLAY_QUESTION" ...
              Case "NAVIGATE"/"NAVIGATE_CYCLING"/"OPEN_MODAL"/"CALL_SERVER" ...
              Case "SET_DISABLED"/"SET_VISIBILITY"/"SET_REQUIRED"/"SET_TEXT" ...
              Case "BUILD_TREE"/"UPDATE_TREENODETEXT"/"REFRESH_LIST" ...
            End Select
      Next
End Sub
explanation: This is the heart of the legacy client: the server never returns HTML, it returns a queue of imperative commands and this loop applies them to the live IE DOM (control combos, labels, tree frame, modals). In React it becomes a pure dispatcher/reducer over a TYPED command array that writes to Zustand stores (page-store for controls, browser-command-store for the modal/window queue, window-manager for windows) instead of poking document.all/frames directly. The 'resfil' response-filter - where a DISPLAY_QUESTION's answer gates which later commands run - is preserved by threading a filter value through the loop; the many *_PARENT variants (which reach into window.frames('main')) collapse because React has one component tree, not nested framesets. Status is scaffolded: dispatch.ts exists and handles the SET_* control verbs, but the navigation (NAVIGATE_CYCLING/CALL_SERVER re-entrancy via mblnDoBrowserCommands), modal, combo-loading, tree, and REFRESH_LIST verbs are not fully built, and IE-only mechanics (showModalDialog, MSXML DOMDocument, cross-frame reach) are being eliminated rather than ported.

name: FillComboList
purpose: Populates an AQS Combo/KPCombo dropdown by reading <item> nodes out of the XML island and imperatively adding each text/value pair to the control, plus an optional leading "NONE" (showzero) entry.

      Case "DISABLED": If Not .enabled -> "T" else "F"

name: GetControlValue
purpose: The generic getter for a control's current value, switching on control type (Protoview date/numeric, tree sentinel, DIV innerText, checkbox YES/NO, XMLLIST action, combo/select/input/textarea) to return the right "L"/text value.
legacy:
Function GetControlValue(ByRef objControl)
  Select Case UCase(objControl.tagname)
    Case "OBJECT": vntValue = .datestring / .text / "tree"   'per CLSID
    Case "DIV": vntValue = .innerText
    Case "ICHECKBOX"/"INPUT type=CHECKBOX": If .checked -> "YES" else "NO"
    Case "XMLLIST": vntValue = .action
    Case "COMBO","KPCOMBO": vntValue = .text
    Case "INPUT": Select Case UCase(.type) 'TEXT/PASSWORD/... -> .value
    Case "SELECT": vntValue = .options(.selectedIndex).text
    Case "TEXTAREA": vntValue = .value
  End Select
  GetControlValue = vntValue
End Function
explanation: This is the value-side twin of GetControlAttribute: because every control type stored its value differently (Protoview datestring, tree sentinel "tree", DIV innerText, checkbox->YES/NO, SELECT selected-option text, INPUT by input-type), a big switch was needed to read one value. In the SPA there is a single source of truth: ControlDef.value in the page-store, kept live by setValue, and executeAction assembles the server payload directly from it (execute-action.ts lines 27-29). No per-tagname extraction is required, so this is eliminated.

name: OnKeyPressHandler

name: OnKeyUpHandler

name: PreProcess

purpose: Looks up all <call> subroutines of a given type (e.g. browser_windowonload, or a compound tab|matchcode=tabins) declared in the page's XML data island and Execute's each named subroutine in document order, letting the server-authored page drive which browser-side procedures run.

Status is design: dispatch.ts is scaffolded for verb commands, but this page-declared procedure runner and its handler registry are not built.

name: SetArrayData

name: SetControlValue
purpose: The single, generic entry point for writing a value into ANY control, branching on control type so each widget's peculiar 'value' property is set correctly, and mirroring the value back into the in-memory XML document.

name: BuildTab
purpose: Lazily builds the HTML for a tab the first time the user clicks it: if the selected tab is still empty, run an XSLT transform of the page's control XML into HTML, inject it, then populate the new controls with their data.

  If intIndex = 0 Then Exit Sub                      'tab 0 already built at load
  If Len(.divTab(intIndex).innerHTML) > 0 Then Exit Sub  'already built once
  Set mxmlStyle = FreeThreadedDOMDocument : mxmlStyle.load "...Controls_ISLLSYS_20010101.xsl"

The MSXML XSLTemplate/processor machinery and the Controls_*.xsl stylesheet are eliminated: the transform becomes JSX in FormRenderer, and GetXMLData's value fill becomes reading from page-store. name: UnEscapeTextValueForXML
purpose: Reverses a home-grown escaping scheme, turning placeholder tokens back into the real characters they stand for (apostrophe, less-than, greater-than, ampersand).

    strToEscape,"#http39;","'"),"#http60;","<"),"#http62;",">"),"#http38;","&")

The React app talks to the backend in JSON, which carries these characters literally and needs no such tokenization, so the routine is eliminated. It is only worth keeping a tiny equivalent util if legacy-encoded data still flows through some unmodernized endpoint.

The showzero shift also ties into SetControlValue's index handling (an extra placeholder row offsets list indices by one). It is not implemented in the POC yet, so this is a plan.

name: ClearXMLDetail
purpose: Removes one or more named items from the session's XML 'detail' blob, then normalizes the resulting string (single-quote the double quotes, strip CR/LF); returns True on success.

Function ClearXMLDetail(ByVal arrXMLDetail)
  Set xmlSessionXML = DOMDocument.6.0
  If xmlSessionXML.loadXML(mstrXMLDetail)=False Then Exit Function
  For x = 0 To Ubound(arrXMLDetail)
    Set nodItem = xmlSessionXML.selectSingleNode("//item[@name='" & arrXMLDetail(x) & "']")
    If Not nodItem Is Nothing Then xmlSessionXML.documentElement.removeChild nodItem
  Next
  mstrXMLDetail = xmlSessionXML.xml
  mstrXMLDetail = Replace(mstrXMLDetail, Chr(34), "'")   'quotes
  mstrXMLDetail = Replace(mstrXMLDetail, Chr(10), "") : Replace(...,Chr(13),"")  'CR/LF
  ClearXMLDetail = True
End Function
explanation: mstrXMLDetail is a session-scoped XML string (note the TrapASPError call -- this runs server/ASP-side) holding named detail items; clearing some means DOM-parsing the string, deleting matching <item name='...'> nodes, and re-serializing, with the quote/CR-LF scrubbing needed only because the result is re-embedded into other markup. In React, session detail is a plain object in app-store, so 'clear these items' is just deleting keys, and all the parse/serialize/escape ceremony is eliminated. This is not built in the POC; it is a plan for where the equivalent state and mutation would live.
